definitions.explanation: The remaining base of a tree after it has been cut down.

examples.japanese: {切|き}り{株|かぶ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}った→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。
examples.english: I sat on a tree stump.
Many tree stumps remained in the forest.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{切|き}り{株|かぶ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧キノコ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|は}えていた→生える：02392_haeru⟧。
examples.english: Mushrooms were growing from an old tree stump.

notes:
{切|き}り{株|かぶ} refers to the part of a tree left standing in the ground after the trunk has been cut down.

FORMS:
{切|き}り (from ⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧, to cut) + ⟦{株|かぶ}→株：02592_kabu⟧ (stump, root stock). The ⟦{株|かぶ}→株：02592_kabu⟧ component here means the base or root portion of a plant.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{株|かぶ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{腰掛|こしか}ける→腰掛ける：13945_koshikakeru⟧: to sit on a stump
- {切|き}り{株|かぶ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧: to pull out a stump
- ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{切|き}り{株|かぶ}: an old stump
- {切|き}り{株|かぶ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{芽|め}→芽：02141_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: sprouts growing from a stump

CULTURAL NOTE:
Tree stumps appear frequently in Japanese folktales and children's stories, often as resting spots for forest animals. The Aesop-derived story 「{待|ま}ちぼうけ」 features a farmer who waits by a stump for another rabbit to crash into it.
